title: Heat Index — the National Weather Service equation, charted
description: The heat index algorithm exactly as the NWS Weather Prediction Center describes it. A simple Steadman-style estimate comes first; if it reaches 80 °F, the page switches to the Rothfusz regression and applies the low-humidity or high-humidity adjustment where one applies, and it shows each step. A temperature × humidity heat map colours the whole plane by the NWS caution, extreme caution, danger and extreme danger bands. It works in °F or °C and has an Austin summer-afternoon preset.
prompt: Build a heat index page that implements the National Weather Service algorithm exactly as the NWS/WPC page describes it. Start with the simple Steadman-style formula averaged with T. If that result is 80°F or more, use the full Rothfusz regression, with the low-humidity adjustment (RH < 13% and 80–112°F) and the high-humidity adjustment (RH > 85% and 80–87°F). Include a temperature × humidity heat map coloured by the NWS caution / extreme caution / danger / extreme danger bands, an Austin summer-afternoon preset, and °F/°C. The spec should implement the algorithm itself and check known values, e.g. T=90°F, RH=70% gives about 105–106°F. Check the coefficients carefully.

methodology: Independent oracle: the spec has its own copy of the NWS algorithm, with the Rothfusz coefficients written in scientific notation so that it isn't a copy-paste of the page's. It compares the page's result, method and band at about 1,900 points from 50 to 120 °F and 0 to 100 % RH, to 1e-9.
Published reference values: 90 °F at 70 % must read 106 °F (the regression gives 105.9), and the page's rounded values must match the NWS chart's 40 % humidity row from 80 to 110 °F exactly.

Each branch has its own test. Below 80 °F the simple estimate is used and the regression is marked as not needed (80 °F at 40 % gives 79.58, just under). The low-humidity adjustment is checked at 100 °F and 5 % (−1.68 °F), and the high-humidity one at 82 °F and 95 % (exactly +1.00 °F). Just outside each window (RH = 13 %, 114 °F, RH = 85 %, 88 °F) no adjustment may apply.

Heat map as data: every one of the 357 cells carries its temperature, RH and band, and each band must equal the oracle's. All five bands must appear on the map, and tapping a cell loads its values into the inputs.

Units and input: °C mode converts the input (98 °F shows as 36.7 °C) and the output while still computing in °F, and switching back returns the same value. Arrow keys on the sliders move the value one step at a time.
risks: A single mistyped coefficient would still produce plausible numbers. The dense oracle sweep and the published 40 % chart row are there to catch that.
The NWS wording ("the simple formula ... averaged with the temperature") is ambiguous. The page uses HI = ½[T + 61 + 1.2(T − 68) + 0.094 RH], and says so on the page.
The printed NWS chart appears to leave out the high-humidity adjustment at 100 % RH, so it differs from the algorithm by 1–2 °F there. The spec uses the 40 % row, where no adjustment applies.
Band edges: the page bands the unrounded value (103.0 is danger), so a reading that rounds to 103 can still be extreme caution at 102.6.
qa.playwright: Most of the work happens in one page.evaluate call that sends about 1,900 (T, RH) pairs to window.__heat.compute and gets the results back in a single round trip. Driving the UI for each point would have taken minutes. The heat map is an SVG with data attributes, so locator.evaluateAll reads all 357 cells at once and the spec checks them against the oracle, not a screenshot. fill() plus Enter works the same on the desktop and Pixel 7 projects. The slider test uses focus() and keyboard.press, since dragging a range thumb is fragile on touch emulation. One downside: the oracle sweep only checks the hook, so the formatted text is covered separately by a handful of UI tests.
coverage: Oracle sweep of the algorithm, method and band across the whole plane
Simple branch below 80 °F; low-humidity and high-humidity adjustments and their edges
Heat map band colours, all five bands, tap to load, marker
Austin preset (danger band), °C conversion both ways, slider keyboard steps, live region

a11y: All inputs are labelled native controls. Each slider is paired with a number field, and the presets and unit choice are toggle buttons with aria-pressed. The result box is an aria-live region that states the value and band in words, so it doesn't rely on colour. The heat map's aria-label describes the current conditions and band, and a text table gives the heat index across temperatures at the chosen humidity.
